internal.title: High CPU Load Caused Increased Latency in Ad Service
internal.body: On 2026-11-08 at 10:37 UTC, the ad service triggered a ServiceLatencyHigh alert due to very high CPU utilization (0.98) coinciding with the enabling of the adHighCpu flag. This caused increased latency but did not significantly affect error rates. The diagnosis confirmed CPU saturation as the root cause. At 10:57 UTC, the flag was disabled, leading to recovery and normalization of service latency and error rates. The incident was resolved promptly with no lasting impact on service availability or error rates.

external.title: Increased Latency in Ad Service Resolved
external.body: Between 10:37 and 10:57 UTC on 2026-11-08, the ad service experienced increased latency. This was identified and resolved by our operations team, restoring normal service performance. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

output.summary: The ad service experienced increased latency due to high CPU load caused by a configuration flag. Disabling the flag restored normal service performance.
output.impact: Customers experienced increased latency in the ad service between 10:37 and 10:57 UTC. There was no significant increase in error rates or service downtime.
output.root_cause: High CPU utilization in the ad service caused by the enabling of a configuration flag (adHighCpu) led to CPU saturation and increased latency.
output.resolution: The configuration flag causing high CPU load was disabled at 10:57 UTC, resulting in recovery of normal service latency and error rates.

lessons.lesson: Monitor CPU utilization closely when enabling new configuration flags that can impact resource usage. Implement gradual rollout and automated rollback mechanisms for such flags.
lessons.applies_when: When a configuration flag that can increase CPU load is enabled in the ad service.

action_items: Implement gradual rollout and automated rollback for configuration flags affecting CPU usage.
Enhance monitoring and alerting on CPU utilization spikes related to configuration changes.
